about: The demo world the seed tool makes (T6.1, K101): one learner, three goals with their concepts, edges and campaign progress, three Companions and the published atoms of their daily doses. Taken from the approved mockup (Version 6, K86): HOOK_MAP 2640, ATLAS 2681, COMP_SHEETS 2810, DOSE 2978, CX_DOSE_Q 3091, DASH 5089. AI-made records are NOT here: prepared-choices.json lists them and the golden run makes them. Keys are the prepared-choice list's world keys (a superset of them). Ids: the tenant and the learner are fixed (INTERFACES.md section 6); every API-made record gets its id from the product and the seed tool writes it to seed-ids.json; SQL-made rows use fixed UUIDv7s the seed tool derives from the key. Content stays English (K41); text marked authored by the orchestrator awaits the owner's fact review (T6.6).

how_made.order_rule: Production's reads list goals, concepts and edges NEWEST FIRST (consumption repo/pg goal.go:230-237, concept_node.go:194-202, concept_edge.go:196-205), and the lens lays children out in the order edges arrive (kiosk-web concept-lens.ts:205-224). So the seed creates goals, concepts and edges in REVERSE of this file's order, one call at a time, and every read returns them in this file's order, the mockup's.

tenant.path: SQL as chora_tenancy_app_rw: INSERT INTO tenants (tenant_id, name); no RLS, status defaults to active. Migration 0021's platform tenant stays (K130).

learner.path: SQL as chora_identity_app_rw, one transaction with chora.tenant_id and chora.user_gcid set: users (gcid, email, identity_provider 'oidc', federated_subject 'kiosk:apollo-visitor'); one tenant_memberships row per role; user_mana with a generous balance and one 'promo' credit in mana_ledger (recorded now: the ledger is partitioned by month from its migration). No API makes them on the kiosk.

dashboard.step: dashboard (after the owner's review, just before the snapshot)
dashboard.path: SQL: user_mana.balance_units to learner.dashboard.mana with one debit ledger entry, and learner_streaks to learner.dashboard.streak_days with the last activity on the snapshot's UTC day (K131 then adds 1 on an event day's first dose open). A visit's LIVE presses cost 0 to 20 mana each (identity migrations 0009, 0023, 0024) and every reset restores the snapshot.

atom.step: api-world, FIRST: before any goal, concept or Companion exists
atom.path: POST /api/atoms {question_type 'mcq', title, stem, body, tags: [topic]}, no cognitive_level (a set level that differs from the serve rung's label is excluded from the campaign lane, dose_campaign_wiring.go:272-274); wait for its atom_index row; POST /api/atoms/{id}/questions {type 'mcq', prompt: the stem, mcq_payload.options [{label, is_correct, explainer}]}, the explanation on the correct option only (the server shuffles the options, questions_handler.go:1113-1116); POST /api/atoms/{id}/publish; wait until atom_index reads it published WITH its served answer key and topic tag (the question POST re-emits atom.created carrying both, outside the outbox, questions_handler.go:89-119). All atoms first because in production each atom.published fans out kg-explorer suggestion requests for won focal concepts in Companion-attached goals (consumption atom_refresh_wiring.go:56); the kiosk edition no longer wires that fan-out (consumption cmd/server/kiosk.go:208-220), so the order is kept as a second guard. The publish embeds the atom on Vertex after it answers and only logs a failure, so api-world waits for every atom's chora_creation.atom_embeddings row. Needs T1.4b's atom-created and atom-published subscriptions (FINDINGS S3); atom.published updates only an existing atom_index row.

concept.path: POST /api/v1/me/concept-graph/concepts {title, atomRefs}, atomRefs = the atoms whose concept this is; concept_key is production's slug of the title. Reverse order (order_rule).

edge.path: POST /api/v1/me/concept-graph/edges {sourceConceptId, targetConceptId, class}: kind hierarchy is 'hierarchy' (source parent, target child), kind link is 'lateral' (concept_graph/edge.go:16-19; lateral edges never add subtree members). Reverse order (order_rule). K188 (21 Oct): the world holds no link edges; every map is a pure tree.

goal.path: POST /api/v1/me/goals {kind 'curiosity', conceptSet: its concepts' keys, northStarNote: the root's title (as production's createMap sends it), rootConceptId} after its concepts and edges, in reverse order (order_rule). Then the Companions, then each goal's march by POST /api/v1/me/goals/{id}/campaign/focus {conceptId} (in the root's subtree; no won check), again in reverse, water's last: the focus retargets the attached Companion's resonance (goals_campaign_handler.go:232-241; acquire never sets it), and the active Companion is the one on the most recently updated goal (consumption subscribers/companion_resolver.go:82-110), so water's focus is the last goal update of all.

companion.path: POST /api/v1/me/companions/acquire {goalId, companionName, species, mode 'dev_hatched'} (no mana; stage 1, 2 slots; attaches the goal; dev_hatched is accepted in every edition, acquisition.go:13-28): Nova, then Ember, then Pingu, after every goal and before any march. Then SQL: companion_instances growth_exp and growth_stage, skill_slots_unlocked = stage + 1, evolution_tier, the species-path skill grants of every stage reached (unequipped), one 'admin_grant' row in companion_growth_events; NO companion_growth_daily_counters rows, so the golden run's first dose open credits Pingu +2 (K102).

campaign.path: SQL campaign_node_progress, one live row per concept with campaign state: won = rungs_cleared 6, six rung_cleared_at stamps ending at won_at (the won_on date), current_rung_correct 0; climbing = rungs_cleared n with n stamps, current_rung_correct = counted, won_at NULL, last_advance_date before the seed's UTC day (a rung clears only on a later UTC day than the last advance); state none = no row.

retention.path: SQL topic_retention keyed by each climbing concept's concept_key, strength 60, last_reviewed_at = the seed time: R = exp(-days/strength) stays at 0.6 or above for 30 days, so no climbing hex cools and every serve climbs (maps_cooling.go; topic_retention.go:111-117, 0.6).

cues.path: SQL learner_weakness: shaky = an active row whose target_concept_id is the concept; due = an active row with a retention row of its own (topic_id = the row's id) below 0.6 for the whole window, apart from the concept-key row that keeps the hex from cooling; mastered = a 'grown' row on the concept's key. Each row needs concept_label and a 768-wide concept_embedding (NOT NULL; how the seed makes it is T6.2's choice). Production's lens draws a due concept shaky as well (concept-lens.ts:578-590).

dose.path: Each goal's dose universe is exactly its five card atoms (bound to its concepts; no learning paths). Review: one sm2_states row, for the review atom only (easiness 1.3, interval 1, last reviewed 3 days before the seed: decay above 0.4 throughout). Stretch: an active growth edge whose cached_drill_atom_ids hold the stretch atom (growth edges own the slot whenever any active row exists, daily_dose.go:435-440); for Urban heat and Food safety that edge matches no concept on the map (the mockup draws no cue there). Campaign: the march's two atoms (DOSE_COMPOSER_V2_ENABLED, F13; T2.18). Curiosity: the remaining atom, through the fresh top-up. T6.4 checks every event date.

atoms.title: The Four National Taps
atoms.body: Singapore draws its water from four sources: local catchment, imported water, NEWater and desalinated water.

mcq.stem: Which of these is not one of Singapore’s Four National Taps?
options: Local catchment
Imported water
Desalinated water
Groundwater wells
mcq.explanation: The four taps are local catchment, imported water, NEWater and desalinated water. Groundwater wells are not one of them.

atoms.title: Water from Johor
atoms.body: Singapore buys part of its water from Johor in Malaysia, under a water agreement that runs until 2061.

mcq.stem: Singapore’s remaining water agreement with Malaysia runs until which year?
mcq.explanation: The 1962 Water Agreement with Malaysia ends in 2061, which is one reason Singapore builds its other taps.

uses: draft.water.q3 (the open question with its picture)

atoms.title: A reservoir in the city centre
atoms.body: Marina Reservoir sits right in the city centre. It was made by building a barrage across the mouth of the Marina Channel.

mcq.stem: How was Marina Reservoir in the city centre made?
options: By digging a new lake in the middle of the island
By building a barrage across the mouth of the Marina Channel
By filling an old quarry with seawater
By joining two rivers in the north
mcq.explanation: A barrage built across the mouth of the Marina Channel turned it into a reservoir right in the city centre.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: More than a water store
atoms.body: The Marina Barrage also keeps out the sea, which helps reduce flooding in the low-lying parts of the city.

mcq.stem: Besides holding water for the city, what else does the Marina Barrage do?
options: It turns seawater into drinking water
It makes electricity from the waves
It keeps out the sea and helps reduce flooding in low-lying areas
It cools the buildings around Marina Bay
mcq.explanation: The barrage keeps out the sea, which helps reduce flooding in the low-lying parts of the city.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: Catching the rain
atoms.body: About two thirds of Singapore’s land collects rainwater, and drains and canals carry it to the reservoirs.

mcq.stem: About how much of Singapore’s land collects rainwater for its water supply?
options: About a tenth
About a third
About two thirds
Nearly all of it
mcq.explanation: About two thirds of Singapore’s land is water catchment; drains and canals carry the rain to the reservoirs.

atoms.title: How mangroves guard the coast
atoms.body: Mangrove roots hold the mud and soften the waves, which protects the shore from erosion.

mcq.stem: How do mangroves help protect Singapore’s coast?
options: They pump seawater back out to sea
Their roots hold the mud and soften the waves
They raise the land a little every year
They keep fish away from the shore
mcq.explanation: Mangrove roots trap mud and break the force of the waves, which slows erosion along the shore.

atoms.title: Why a city runs warm
atoms.body: Roads and buildings soak up the sun and give off heat, while trees and plants shade the ground and help cool it.

mcq.stem: Which of these helps cool a hot street in the city?
options: More dark roads and car parks
Bigger glass walls facing the sun
Trees that shade the ground
Fewer plants along the pavement
mcq.explanation: Roads and buildings soak up the sun and give off heat; trees shade the ground and cool the air around them.

atoms.title: Why the otters came back
atoms.body: Otters mostly eat fish, so seeing them again is a sign that the rivers and reservoirs are healthier.

mcq.stem: What does the return of otters tell us about Singapore’s rivers and reservoirs?
options: They are too salty for fish
They have been drained for building
They are closed to all animals
They are healthier, with enough fish for the otters to eat
mcq.explanation: Otters mostly eat fish, so seeing them again is a sign that the rivers and reservoirs are healthier.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: Otters in the city
atoms.body: Otter families are now often seen along rivers, reservoirs and the coast, even close to the city centre.

mcq.stem: Where are otter families often seen in Singapore today?
options: Along rivers, reservoirs and the coast, even near the city centre
Only inside the zoo
Only on islands far from the mainland
Only deep inside the nature reserves
mcq.explanation: Otter families now often turn up along rivers, reservoirs and the coast, even close to the city centre.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: Green paths between parks
atoms.body: Park connectors are paths that link parks and green spaces across the island, for walking and cycling.

mcq.stem: What does Singapore’s Park Connector Network link up?
options: Parks and green spaces across the island
Reservoirs and the sea
Schools and shopping malls
Hawker centres and MRT stations
mcq.explanation: Park connectors link parks and green spaces across Singapore, so people can walk and cycle between them.

atoms.title: Why hawker centres were built
atoms.body: From the 1970s, street hawkers moved into purpose-built centres with water, drainage and licences.

mcq.stem: Why did Singapore move street hawkers into hawker centres from the 1970s?
options: To turn the stalls into restaurants
To close down street food for good
To serve only tourists
To give hawkers clean water, drainage and licences
mcq.explanation: Purpose-built centres gave hawkers clean water, proper drainage and licences, which made street food cleaner and safer.

atoms.title: Keeping hawker food safe
atoms.body: Hawker stalls need a licence, and the clean water and drainage at hawker centres help keep the food safe.

mcq.stem: What must a hawker stall have before it can sell food?
options: A licence
A website
A delivery van
Its own dining hall
mcq.explanation: Every hawker stall needs a licence, and the clean water and drainage at hawker centres help keep the food safe.

atoms.title: A living heritage
atoms.body: UNESCO added Singapore’s hawker culture to its list of intangible cultural heritage in December 2020.

mcq.stem: What did UNESCO do for Singapore’s hawker culture in December 2020?
options: It named it the world’s cheapest food
It closed the oldest hawker centres
It added it to its list of intangible cultural heritage
It moved the hawkers into restaurants
mcq.explanation: In December 2020 UNESCO added Singapore’s hawker culture to its list of intangible cultural heritage.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: Why UNESCO listed it
atoms.body: It is a living tradition: hawkers pass their recipes down, and people from every community eat side by side.

mcq.stem: Why does UNESCO call hawker culture a living tradition?
options: Every hawker centre is more than a hundred years old
Hawkers pass their recipes down, and people from every community eat side by side
Hawker food is cooked only on special holidays
Only tourists are allowed to eat there
mcq.explanation: Hawkers pass their recipes down through the generations, and people from every community eat side by side.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: A hawker favourite
atoms.body: Chicken rice, tender chicken served with rice cooked in chicken stock, is one of the best-known hawker dishes.

mcq.stem: What gives the rice in chicken rice its flavour?
options: It is fried with chilli
It is cooked in chicken stock
It is steamed in coconut milk
It is soaked in soy sauce
mcq.explanation: The rice is cooked in chicken stock, often with garlic and ginger, which gives it its rich flavour.

atoms.title: How used water becomes NEWater
atoms.body: NEWater starts as used water. After treatment at a water reclamation plant, it is cleaned in three steps: microfiltration strains out fine particles and germs, reverse osmosis pushes the water through a membrane that holds back dissolved salts, and ultraviolet light destroys any germs that are left.

mcq.stem: After the water reclamation plant, in what order is used water cleaned to make NEWater?
options: Reverse osmosis, then UV light, then microfiltration
Microfiltration, then reverse osmosis, then UV light
UV light, then microfiltration, then reverse osmosis
Microfiltration, then UV light, then reverse osmosis
mcq.explanation: Microfiltration strains out fine particles first, reverse osmosis then holds back dissolved salts, and UV light destroys any germs that are left.

atoms.title: Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve
atoms.body: Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve, in the north-west of Singapore, protects mangroves and mudflats. Every year, from about September to March, migratory shorebirds stop there to rest and feed on their long journeys.

mcq.stem: When do migratory shorebirds stop at Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve?
options: Only once every ten years
Only in June
Every year, from about September to March
Every night of the year
mcq.explanation: From about September to March each year, migratory shorebirds stop at Sungei Buloh to rest and feed.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: Kaya toast
atoms.body: Kaya toast is a classic Singapore breakfast: toasted bread with kaya and butter, often eaten with soft-boiled eggs and a cup of kopi. Kaya is a sweet jam of coconut milk, eggs and sugar, often flavoured with pandan leaves.

mcq.stem: What is kaya toast often eaten with at breakfast?
options: Fried rice and soup
Ice cream and fruit
Noodles and curry
Soft-boiled eggs and a cup of kopi
mcq.explanation: Kaya toast is often eaten with soft-boiled eggs and a cup of kopi.

atoms.authored: orchestrator, for the owner's fact review

atoms.title: Teh tarik
atoms.body: Teh tarik is hot tea with condensed milk. “Tarik” means “pull” in Malay: the tea is poured back and forth between two mugs from a height, which mixes in the milk, cools the tea and gives it a frothy top.

mcq.stem: What does “tarik” mean in teh tarik?
options: Sweet
Pull
Hot
Milk
mcq.explanation: “Tarik” means “pull” in Malay, after the way the tea is poured back and forth between two mugs.
